content:
The first release candidate v4.8.0-rc1 for the v4.8.0 release of Lean is available now.

This release brings:

  • Functional induction principles
  • Improved termination checking
  • Shorter instance names!
  • Changes to typeclass search that should reduce unnecessary backtracking
  • Fewer Nat.succs, after induction and simplifying!
  • more universe constraint approximations
  • Many improvements to pretty printing
  • rw? is available to everyone, and doesn't require a pre-built cache
  • Elaboration diagnostics available via set_option diagnostics true in
  • More flexibility with the irreducible attribute (now usable locally and in scopes).
  • Changes to the isDefEq algorithm
    • Not everything is good news here: in fact Mathlib has become about 5% slower upon moving to v4.8.0-rc1.
    • We're confident however that we're moving in the right direction and laying a foundation for future speed ups.
    • We're hopeful that the new diagnostic tools will enable significant speed-ups across Mathlib in the near future.
    • We'll write more about the changes, and diagnostic tools, later.
  • A substantial revamp to Lake's internals, and output. lean4#3835

and many bug fixes and documentation improvements to Lean and Lake.

Std, Aesop, ProofWidgets, and Mathlib, have moved their development branches to v4.8.0-rc1, and lean4checkeris available, too, so please go try out the new goodies!

This is a release candidate, so please expect some rough edges. Please report any issues you find! If anyone finds anything that is a regression relative to v4.7.0, we will likely make a new release candidate. Otherwise, we hope for this to become v4.8.0 at the end of May.
This is a fantastic release, even by Lean standards! Thanks a lot to everybody involved!

Something important I forgot to announce here: v4.8.0-rc1 brings support for lakefile.toml as a simpler configuration file instead of lakefile.lean.

Complex projects will continue to use lakefile.lean, as the toml format is not yet as expressive. However we will continue expanding the scope of what can be done from a toml file. Simpler projects should already be able to switch. There is a migration assistant available via lake translate-config toml (although note comments will be dropped, so please review carefully). See https://github.com/leanprover-community/import-graph/pull/5 for an example of switching.

(Further discussion in the discussion thread.)
